input: The schedule float for the upgrade project has been set at 9%, and this figure is defended here against the lower alternative that has been proposed. It is important to understand that float is not a contingency for scope growth; rather, it represents time that is held against the delays that tend to arise within the approved scope itself, such as late deliveries, poor weather at the tie-in windows, and work fronts that open later than the programme assumes because the plant they attach to is still in operation. The cost table in the Costs section prices the programme on the basis of the stated float, so the float and the price effectively stand or fall together: a programme priced on a shorter float would carry delay costs that the table does not show, because extended preliminaries and re-sequenced work are charged by the week. The steering group set the float after recent shutdown tie-ins overran their windows for reasons that were entirely within the approved scope, and FID is taken on the programme as priced, with the float included within it; reducing the float in order to present a lower headline figure would simply move the same cost into overrun, where it would be paid with less control and
